narrative:
The model gives you a 45% chance of failing your final year. That is not a certainty, but it is high enough that the model has flagged you as needing remedial courses rather than waiting until the end of the year.

The strongest reason was your intention about continuing into higher education. You said you do not want higher education, while every student who passed in this data did want it. This was the main factor pushing the prediction toward failing. The next two most important factors actually worked in your favor: you have no past class failures, which matches the passing average, and your weekend alcohol consumption is very low. Both nudged the prediction toward passing, but they were less influential than your education intention.

To improve your chances, reconsider whether higher education is part of your plan and discuss this with your family or guardian. Keep your record free of failures and keep weekend drinking very low. Also increase your weekly study time: you currently study under two hours, while most passing students study two to five hours or more. Your six absences are above the passing average of about four, so improving attendance would help too.
